expected.reason: 19 non-member PRs were landed by pytorchmergebot (closed with a commit) in the two days the recording covers, from 14 people, including some who look like real outsiders (e.g. AMD engineers, first-time authors).
expected.judgment_call: The 200-PR sample covers only ~2 days and many of the landed CONTRIBUTOR authors are PyTorch staff whose org membership isn't public (huydhn, drisspg, eellison…). 'Worth' rests on PyTorch's well-known record of merging outside work, which this sample shows only faintly; 'Not enough evidence' from this sample alone would also be defensible.

expected.judgment_call: Most closed PRs were unrequested drive-by or AI-generated changes, so a careful contributor who opens an issue first may do much better than 3%. But the history shows no working path for newcomers, and the audit's 5% merge-rate floor would fail it.
